$schema_note: Phase 0 proof-of-concept dataset for the billionaire-government-money profile (docs/ideas/billionaire-subsidy-tracker.md). Subject is a named living person: every figure is source-linked. The unit of truth is the COMPANY and the AWARD; the person is a lens (founder + controlling shareholder + CEO). Money TYPE values: FEDERAL_CONTRACT, FEDERAL_GRANT, FEDERAL_LOAN, TAX_CREDIT_SUBSIDY, STATE_LOCAL_SUBSIDY, REGULATORY_CREDIT. POLITICAL_SPENDING is money flowing OUT from Musk, tracked here for the side-by-side, and is NOT government money received.
subject: Elon Musk

headline.label: at least $38 billion
headline.description: Lifetime U.S. federal and local government contracts, loans, subsidies, and tax credits to Musk's companies (Tesla, SpaceX, X Corp.) over more than 20 years, per a Washington Post analysis built on Good Jobs First + USAspending + FPDS + SEC data.
headline.composition: more than 400 federal contracts, nearly 90 federal and local grants, more than two-dozen tax credits or property-tax abatements, and six loans
caveats: The Post calls it a floor ('at least $38B'): it includes only publicly available records and OMITS classified defense/intelligence work (e.g., a SpaceX/NRO spy-satellite contract reported at ~$1.8B is excluded).
Some grants/tax credits had unavailable dollar amounts, further understating the total.
Mixes already-paid funds with committed/promised funds; it is 'funding directed to' the companies, not strictly cash-in-hand.
A separate ~$11.8B in potential future payments across 52 ongoing contracts is NOT part of the $38B.

line_items.value_basis: initial minimum IDIQ value; task orders grew over the contract's life
line_items.notes: Fixed-price IDIQ. Later CRS-2 round (awarded 2016) added more SpaceX revenue not separately broken out here.

line_items.value_basis: firm-fixed-price total contract value, contingent on completing test flights and six operational missions

line_items.notes: Verified verbatim against the NASA primary source: 'The firm-fixed price, milestone-based contract total award value is $2.89 billion.' GAO denied competitor protests July 30, 2021.

line_items.value_basis: contract modification value

line_items.notes: Ceiling value. Subsequent FY2026 task orders (Oct 2025) assigned SpaceX 5 missions for $714M.

line_items.value_basis: Reuters-sourced estimate of classified value; NOT in public USAspending data
line_items.notes: CONTESTED/CLASSIFIED. Figure is Reuters' sourcing, not an official release. This is the item the Washington Post explicitly EXCLUDED from the $38B as classified work — so it should NOT be double-counted into the headline; listed here separately for completeness.

line_items.time_period: 2010 (loan closed Jan 2010; repaid in full May 22, 2013)
line_items.description: U.S. Dept. of Energy Advanced Technology Vehicles Manufacturing (ATVM) loan to develop the Model S and the Fremont, CA manufacturing line; repaid ~9 years early, in full with interest.
line_items.agency: U.S. Department of Energy (Loan Programs Office)
line_items.value_basis: loan commitment; ~$452M actually drawn
line_items.notes: REPAID. Taxpayers earned ~$12M interest (interest-only) / ~$26M total including exit payments (the two figures differ on whether exit/bonus payments are counted). DOE confirms repayment but does NOT publish the profit figure, so the profit number is press-sourced, not official. This is direct government money that was returned with a profit to taxpayers.

line_items.category: Tesla regulatory credits (NOT a direct government payment)
line_items.amount_label: $11.4 billion (cumulative, per WaPo); ~$9B by summing 10-K annuals
line_items.description: Revenue Tesla earned selling regulatory compliance credits (state ZEV + federal GHG/CAFE) to OTHER automakers that fall short of government emissions/efficiency mandates.
line_items.agency: N/A (government-CREATED compliance market; CARB / EPA / NHTSA set the mandates)
line_items.value_basis: WaPo cites $11.4B cumulative; annual audited 10-K figures sum to a broadly consistent ~$9-11B
line_items.critical_nuance: This is the single most important caveat in the dataset. This money flows FROM other automakers TO Tesla inside a government-mandated compliance market. The government creates the market and the obligation but writes Tesla NO check. It is NOT a direct subsidy or government payment. Classify as 'regulatory-market revenue,' not 'government subsidy.' Counting it as 'government money to Musk' is the exact line critics (fairly) attack in the WaPo number.
line_items.forward_note: The 2025 federal tax-and-policy law eliminated the penalties underpinning the ZEV/CAFE credit market; this revenue stream is projected to shrink sharply (2025 already reported down ~28%).

line_items.description: Nevada incentive package to land Tesla's battery Gigafactory in Storey County: sales-tax abatement (~$725M), property-tax abatement (~$332M), transferable tax credits (~$120M), jobs credits (~$75M), and more.
line_items.value_basis: ANNOUNCED/authorized value over 20 years, contingent on performance thresholds; realized value differs
line_items.notes: A separate ~$330M expansion abatement package was approved March 2023 (not included in this $1.3B).

line_items.agency: New York State (Empire State Development / Buffalo Billion)
line_items.value_basis: $750M = core state capital investment; ~$959M when all incentives/infrastructure/tax breaks are included
line_items.notes: $750M vs $959M is a scope difference. Widely criticized as underperforming on promised jobs/output.

line_items.agency: Del Valle ISD (Texas Chapter 313) + Travis County
line_items.value_basis: authorized multi-year value
line_items.notes: Travis County deal reported under review as of Nov 2025.

line_items.description: Texas Enterprise Zone sales-tax refunds for SpaceX Boca Chica/Starbase (up to ~$3.75M GigaBay + up to ~$3.75M Starship expansion), plus a Cameron County property-tax abatement.

line_items.notes: SpaceX's largest government money is federal contracts, not these state/local breaks.

line_items.notes: California also credits Tesla with >$2.48B in ZEV-credit value per Newsom's office, but that is regulatory-market value (see tesla-regulatory-credits), not a direct grant; do not double-count.

line_items.amount_label: at least ~$1.5 billion (state/local) / ~$3.6B combined all-government subsidies+credits
line_items.description: Good Jobs First's documented state/local subsidy component across all Musk companies (~$1.5B), rising to ~$3.6B when various federal+local subsidies and credits are combined.
line_items.agency: Multiple state/local governments (per Good Jobs First Subsidy Tracker)
line_items.value_basis: GJF compiled tally; scope-sensitive
line_items.notes: AGGREGATE — contains the individual state/local items above; do not sum together. Scope discipline: ~$1.5B (state/local) != ~$3.6B (subsidies+credits all levels) != $38B (all-government). The $38B is dominated by federal SpaceX contracts, not state/local incentives.

line_items.category: Consumer tax credit (demand-side, NOT paid to Tesla)
line_items.amount_label: up to $7,500 per vehicle; no official Tesla-buyer cumulative total exists
line_items.description: Federal new-clean-vehicle tax credit (IRC Section 30D). Flows to the BUYER (or, since Jan 1 2024, the dealer as a point-of-sale rebate), not to Tesla — a demand-side subsidy that lowers the price buyers pay for Tesla vehicles.
line_items.value_basis: per-vehicle credit; NO official manufacturer-level cumulative dollar breakdown for Tesla buyers exists
line_items.critical_nuance: DEMAND-SIDE: money does not land on Tesla's books. Treasury/IRS reported $2B+ in point-of-sale EV credits to 300,000+ buyers (all makers) since Jan 2024, and ~87% of 2024 EV sales used the credit, but no reliable figure isolates Tesla buyers' share. Any 'Tesla buyers got $X billion' number is a DERIVED ESTIMATE (sales volume x credit), not official.

line_items.category: Federal manufacturing tax credit (supply-side, paid to Tesla)
line_items.description: IRC Section 45X advanced-manufacturing production credit benefiting Tesla's energy generation & storage segment ($35/kWh cell + $10/kWh module, etc.); recognized partly as a reduction of cost of revenue.
line_items.value_basis: Tesla FY2024 10-K disclosure (energy segment only)
line_items.notes: ENERGY-SEGMENT ONLY. Tesla's 4680 vehicle cells are also 45X-eligible but Tesla does not separately break out an automotive 45X figure, so company-wide 45X is undisclosed and likely higher. Separately, ITEP found Tesla paid $0 federal income tax on $2.3B of 2024 U.S. pretax income, aided by ~$300M in U.S. tax credits.

caveats:
CRITICAL DISTINCTIONS (read before citing any number):

1. GROSS CONTRACT VALUE != SUBSIDY != PROFIT != PERSONAL INCOME. A federal CONTRACT (e.g., SpaceX's NASA/Space Force awards) is the government BUYING a service or good (launches, cargo, a lunar lander) at a negotiated price — it funds operations, payroll, and capital, and most of it is spent delivering the work. A SUBSIDY or tax break (Nevada/NY/Texas abatements) is closer to a gift or a forgone tax — the government gets no direct service in return. A LOAN (the DOE ATVM facility) is money that must be repaid; Tesla repaid its $465M in full, early, with a profit to taxpayers. Never collapse these into one blended 'Musk got $X' figure without breaking down by TYPE and saying plainly that contracts are the government buying things. That blending is exactly what critics (fairly) hit the Washington Post $38B number on.

2. CONTRACTS (services rendered) vs SUBSIDIES (gifts/breaks). The bulk of the $38B headline is federal CONTRACTS to SpaceX — i.e., the government chose SpaceX as the lowest-cost, most-capable launch provider and paid market(ish) rates for services delivered. That is categorically different from a tax abatement handed over to attract a factory. A civic-accountability profile must show the split, not the lump sum.

3. REGULATORY CREDITS ARE NOT GOVERNMENT MONEY. Tesla's $11.4B in regulatory-credit revenue is money paid by OTHER automakers inside a government-CREATED compliance market (state ZEV mandates + federal GHG/CAFE rules). The government sets the rules and creates the market but writes Tesla no check. Listing it as 'government money to Musk' is the single most misleading move available; flag it as regulatory-market revenue every time.

4. CONSUMER EV CREDITS ARE DEMAND-SIDE. The up-to-$7,500 federal EV credit flows to BUYERS (or dealers), not to Tesla's books. It subsidizes demand for Tesla cars but is not a payment to Tesla. No official figure isolates how much went to Tesla buyers; any such number is a derived estimate. (By contrast, the 45X manufacturing credit IS a supply-side credit that hits Tesla's financials — $756M in FY2024 for the energy segment alone.)

5. ANNOUNCED/CEILING != REALIZED. State subsidy packages (Nevada $1.3B, NY $750M) are authorized multi-year ceilings contingent on performance; realized value is lower and disputed. Federal contract 'ceiling' / 'up to' values (NSSL Phase 3 'up to $5.9B') are maximum potential, not obligated dollars.

6. THE $38B IS A FLOOR, AND ALSO MIXES PAID + PROMISED. The Washington Post calls it 'at least $38B': it excludes classified defense/intelligence work (e.g., the ~$1.8B NRO/Starshield contract) and some grants with unavailable amounts, so the true figure is higher. But it also mixes cash already paid with funds committed/promised — so it is 'funding directed to' the companies, not cash-in-hand. A separate ~$11.8B in future contract obligations is NOT part of the $38B.

7. AGGREGATES CONTAIN THEIR LINE ITEMS — DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT. The SpaceX ~$22B cumulative, the GJF ~$1.5B state/local, and the Musk >$290M 2024 totals each CONTAIN the individual items listed under them. Summing the JSON 'amount' fields naively will over-count. Use the headline $38B (or the per-type breakdown) for any total, not a sum of all rows.

8. ATTRIBUTING COMPANY MONEY TO THE PERSON IS DEFENSIBLE BUT IMPERFECT. It is fair to say public money flowed to an empire Musk founded, controls, and runs (founder + controlling shareholder + CEO/chair of SpaceX; founder, largest shareholder, and CEO of Tesla) — WITH the explicit framing that the dollars went to the COMPANIES and the person controls/benefits from them. It is analytically false to imply the dollars landed in Musk's personal account. Tesla in particular is a public company whose subsidies also benefit pension funds, index investors, and millions of small shareholders. The honest unit of truth is the company and the award; the person is a lens layered on top, with the control relationship stated, never an implied wire transfer to a checking account.

9. POLITICAL SPENDING IS MONEY OUT, NOT MONEY IN. The America PAC / RBG PAC / 2026 figures are money Musk SPENT on politics, included for the side-by-side contrast (public money received vs political influence purchased). They are not government money received and must never be added to the $38B.
